title: Bahs va o‘z fikrini himoya qilish
goal_uz: Dars oxirida ingliz tilida o‘z fikringizni aniq bayon qilib, uni dalillar bilan qo‘llab-quvvatlaysiz, qarshi fikrlarga e’tirof va raddiya bilan javob berasiz, dalil so‘ray olasiz va mojarodasiz bahs yuritishni o‘rganasiz.

vocab.uz: e’tirof (qarshi fikrning haq ekanini qabul qilish)

scenes.title: Bugun: bahslashish san’ati
board: State · Support · Concede · Counter · Evidence · Politeness

examples.t: I see your point, but the evidence says otherwise.
examples.uz: Fikringizni tushunaman, ammo dalillar boshqacha ko‘rsatadi.

scenes.say_native: Assalomu alaykum! Oldingi darsda hikoya qilishni o‘rgangan edik. Bugun bahslashishni o‘rganamiz: o‘z fikringizni qanday bayon qilish, uni dalillar bilan qo‘llab-quvvatlash, qarshi fikrni e’tirof etib, keyin raddiya berish, dalil so‘rash va bosim ostida muloyim qolish. IELTS nutqining uchinchi qismida ham, ish intervyularida ham aynan shu ko‘nikma kerak. Boshlaymiz. IELTS ning uchinchi qismida imtihonchi sizning fikringizni emas, qanday himoyalaganingizni baholaydi: tuzilma, ravshanlik va to‘g‘ri iboralar. Shuning uchun bu darsda har bir qadamni alohida o‘rganamiz.
scenes.say: Welcome back! Last time we told stories. Today we argue — how to state your opinion, support it with evidence, concede the other side and then counter it, ask for evidence, and stay polite under pressure. This is exactly what IELTS speaking part three and job interviews test. Let's begin.
scenes.say_uz: Qaytganingiz bilan! O‘tgan darsda hikoya qilishgandi o‘rgandik. Bugun bahslashamiz — fikringizni bayon qilish, uni dalillar bilan qo‘llab-quvvatlash, qarshi fikrni e’tirof etib raddiya berish, dalil so‘rash va bosim ostida muloyim qolish. Bu aynan IELTS nutqi uchinchi qismi va ish intervyulari testi. Boshlaymiz.

scenes.title: Fikringizni bayon qilish

examples.t: I'd argue that public transport should be free.
examples.uz: Jamiyatdagi transport bepul bo‘lishi kerak, deb ta’kidlayman.

scenes.say_native: Fikringizni bayon qilishning ingliz tilidagi iboralari bor: “I strongly believe that…” — men qat’iy ishonaman; “In my view, / From my perspective,” — mening fikrimcha; “It seems to me that…” — menga shunday tuyuladiki; “I’d argue that…” — men shuni ta’kidlayman. O‘zbek tilida ham “Fikrimcha”, “Menimcha”, “Ishonchim komilki” bor — xuddi shunday darajalar. Endi mashq qilamiz. O‘zbek tilida ham shunday darajalar bor: “Ishonchim komilki” — eng kuchli, “Menimcha” — o‘rtacha, “Menga shunday tuyuladiki” — yumshoq. Ingliz tilida ham aynan shu tanlov muhim, chunki suhbatdosh sizning qat’iyatingizni shu orqali baholaydi.
scenes.say: Ways to state your opinion in English: “I strongly believe that…”; “In my view,” or “From my perspective,”; “It seems to me that…”; “I'd argue that…” Uzbek has the same levels — “Fikrimcha,” “Menimcha,” “Ishonchim komilki.” Now practice.
scenes.say_uz: Ingliz tilida fikr bayon qilish iboralari: “I strongly believe that…” — qat’iy ishonaman; “In my view” yoki “From my perspective” — mening fikrimcha; “It seems to me that…” — menga shunday tuyuladiki; “I'd argue that…” — men shuni ta’kidlayman. O‘zbek tilida ham darajalar bor: “Fikrimcha”, “Menimcha”, “Ishonchim komilki”. Endi mashq.

scenes.title: Fikr iboralarini tanlang
board: Say it with three different starters
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Mavzu: masofaviy ish. Bitta fikrni uch xil boshlanish bilan ayting: “I strongly believe that remote work is the future.” “In my view, remote work is the future.” “I’d argue that remote work is the future.” Baland ovozda ayting. Uchchalasi ham to‘g‘ri, lekin “I strongly believe” eng kuchli, “It seems” eng yumshoq — tanlovingiz ishonchingizni ko‘rsatadi.
scenes.say: Topic: remote work. Say “remote work is the future” three ways: “I strongly believe that remote work is the future.” “In my view, remote work is the future.” “I'd argue that remote work is the future.” Aloud.
scenes.say_uz: Mavzu: masofaviy ish. “Remote work is the future” fikrini uch xil ayting: “I strongly believe that…”, “In my view…”, “I'd argue that…” Baland ovozda.

scenes.title: Javoblar
scenes.say_native: Javoblar: uchala boshlanish to‘g‘ri. Kuchli fikr uchun: “I strongly believe”; neytral fikr uchun: “In my view”; tortishuvli fikr uchun: “I’d argue”. Endi fikringizni dalil bilan qo‘llab-quvvatlashni o‘rganamiz.
scenes.say: Answers: all three work. Strong conviction — “I strongly believe”; neutral framing — “In my view”; a debatable position — “I'd argue.” Now supporting your opinion with evidence.
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar: uchalasi ham to‘g‘ri. Kuchli ishonch — “I strongly believe”; neytral — “In my view”; tortishuvli — “I'd argue”. Endi fikringizni dalil bilan qo‘llab-quvvatlash.

scenes.title: Fikringizni dalillar bilan qo‘llab-quvvatlash

examples.t: Because companies save on office costs.

scenes.say_native: Fikrni dalil bilan qo‘llash qoliplari: “Because…” — chunki; “The reason is…” — sababi; “For instance,” yoki “For example,” — masalan; “Research shows that…” — tadqiqotlar shuni ko‘rsatadiki; “According to…” — …ga ko‘ra; “Statistics indicate that…” — statistik ma’lumotlar shuni ko‘rsatadiki. Dalilsiz fikr — faqat da’vo. Endi mashq qilamiz. Mantiqiy zanjirni eslab qoling: da’vo, so‘ng dalil, so‘ng misol. Da’voning o‘zi quruq, dalil uni jonlantiradi. IELTS’da “I think…” dan keyin “because” ishlatmasangiz, ball pastroq baholanadi.
scenes.say: Frames to support an opinion: “Because…”; “The reason is…”; “For instance,” or “For example,”; “Research shows that…”; “According to…”; “Statistics indicate that…” An opinion without evidence is only a claim. Now practice.
scenes.say_uz: Fikrni qo‘llab-quvvatlash qoliplari: “Because…” — chunki; “The reason is…” — sababi; “For instance” yoki “For example” — masalan; “Research shows that…” — tadqiqotlar ko‘rsatadiki; “According to…” — ga ko‘ra; “Statistics indicate that…” — statistikalar. Dalilsiz fikr — shunchaki da’vo. Endi mashq.

scenes.title: Fikrga dalil qo‘shing
board: Add two pieces of evidence, aloud
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Da’vo: “Remote work is the future.” — “Masofaviy ish — kelajak.” Baland ovozda ikki dalil qo‘shing: masalan, kompaniyalar ofis xarajatlarini tejaydi, tadqiqotlar masofaviy xodimlar kamroq charchashini ko‘rsatadi. Ingliz tilida ayting. Ikki xil dalil keltiring: biri statistika, biri shaxsiy misol — suhbatdoshni ikkalasi birga ishontiradi.
scenes.say: Claim: “Remote work is the future.” Add two pieces of evidence aloud — for example, companies save on office costs, and research shows remote workers report less burnout. In English.
scenes.say_uz: Da’vo: “Remote work is the future.” — “Masofaviy ish — kelajak.” Ikki dalil qo‘shing baland ovozda: masalan, kompaniyalar ofis xarajati tejaydi; tadqiqotlar masofaviy xodimlar kamroq charchashini ko‘rsatadi. Ingliz tilida.

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: “Research shows remote staff report less burnout.”
scenes.say_native: Javoblar: “Because companies save on office costs.” va “Research shows remote staff report less burnout.” — ikkala dalil mantiqiy va kuchli. Endi qarshi fikrga e’tirof etishni o‘rganamiz.
scenes.say: Answers: “Because companies save on office costs,” and “Research shows remote staff report less burnout.” Both are logical and strong. Now conceding the other side.
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar: “Because companies save on office costs.” Va “Research shows remote staff report less burnout.” Ikkalasi ham mantiqiy va kuchli. Endi qarshi fikrni e’tirof etish.

scenes.title: E’tirof va raddiya
board: Concede: “You have a point there…” / “Fair enough…”
Counter: “With respect, the data suggests otherwise.”

examples.t: You have a point — however, quality drops without oversight.
examples.uz: Fikringizda jon bor — ammo nazoratsiz sifat pasayadi.

scenes.say_native: E’tirof va raddiya: qarshi fikrning haq bo‘lishi mumkinligini tan oling: “You have a point there.” — “Fikringizda jon bor.” “Fair enough.” — “Mayli, rostdan.” Keyin raddiya bering: “However,…” — “Biroq…” “That said,…” — “Shunday bo‘lsa ham…” “Even so,…” — “Lekin baribir…” Kuchli raddiya: “With respect, the data suggests otherwise.” — “Hurmat bilan, ma’lumotlar aksinchasini ko‘rsatadi.” E’tirofning kuchi shundaki, u suhbatni hamkorlikka aylantiradi: siz raqibingizni tushunganingizni ko‘rsatasiz, keyin o‘z nuqtangizni chiqming. Bunda hech kim yutqazmaydi — ikkala tomon ham hurmat bilan tinglaydi.
scenes.say: Conceding and countering. Accept that the other side has a point: “You have a point there,” “Fair enough.” Then counter: “However,…” “That said,…” “Even so,…” A strong counter: “With respect, the data suggests otherwise.”
scenes.say_uz: E’tirof va raddiya. Qarshi fikrning jon borligini tan oling: “You have a point there.” “Fair enough.” Keyin raddiya: “However,” “That said,” “Even so.” Kuchli raddiya: “With respect, the data suggests otherwise.”

scenes.title: E’tirof + raddiya yozing
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Raqib deydi: “Remote work kills team spirit.” — “Masofaviy ish jamoa ruhini o‘ldiradi.” Baland ovozda e’tirof qilib, keyin raddiya bering: “You have a point — however,…” Birinchi e’tirof gapini “but” yoki “however” bilan boshlang, keyin ikki gap bilan o‘z dalilingizni bering.
scenes.say: Your opponent argues: “Remote work kills team spirit.” Aloud — concede first, then counter: “You have a point — however,…” Make it two sentences.
scenes.say_uz: Raqib aytadi: “Remote work kills team spirit.” — “Masofaviy ish jamoa ruhini o‘ldiradi.” Ovoz chiqarib avval e’tirof, keyin raddiya bering: “You have a point — however,…” Ikki gap.

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: “You have a point — however, many teams bond online just as well.”
“Fair enough, but research shows remote teams can outperform office teams.”
scenes.say_native: Javoblar: “You have a point — however, many teams bond online just as well.” — “Fikringizda jon bor — ammo ko‘plab jamoalar onlaynda ham xuddi shunday bog‘lanadi.” “Fair enough, but research shows remote teams can outperform office teams.” — “Mayli — ammo tadqiqotlar masofaviy jamoalar ofisdagilardan kuchliroq bo‘lishi mumkinligini ko‘rsatadi.” Kuchli. Endi dalil so‘rashni o‘rganamiz.
scenes.say: Answers: “You have a point — however, many teams bond online just as well.” And “Fair enough, but research shows remote teams can outperform office teams.” Strong. Now asking for evidence.
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar: “You have a point — however, many teams bond online just as well.” Va “Fair enough, but research shows remote teams can outperform office teams.” Ikkalasi ham kuchli. Endi dalil so‘rash.

scenes.title: Dalil so‘rash
board: “Is that based on research or personal experience?”

examples.t: What's the evidence for that claim?

scenes.say_native: Dalil so‘rash iboralari: “What’s the evidence for that?” — bu da’voning dalili qanday? “Could you give an example?” — misol keltira olasizmi? “Where does that figure come from?” — bu raqam qayerdan olingan? “Is that based on research or personal experience?” — bu tadqiqotga asoslanganmi yoki shaxsiy tajribaga? Bu savollar sizni professional ko‘rsatadi. Endi mashq qilamiz. Dalil so‘rash hamma vaqt hujum emas: professional muhokamalarda bu odatiy va hurmatga sazovor savol. Hozirgacha mingta uchrashuvda “What’s the evidence?” degan savol ko‘plab yomon qarorlarni to‘xtatgan.
scenes.say: Phrases to ask for evidence: “What's the evidence for that?” “Could you give an example?” “Where does that figure come from?” “Is that based on research or personal experience?” These questions make you sound professional. Now practice.
scenes.say_uz: Dalil so‘rash iboralari: “What's the evidence for that?” “Could you give an example?” “Where does that figure come from?” “Is that based on research or personal experience?” Bu savollar sizni professional ko‘rsatadi. Endi mashq.

scenes.title: Dalil so‘rang
board: Ask for evidence, aloud, three different ways
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Raqib deydi: “Remote workers are less productive.” — “Masofaviy ishchilar kamroq unumdor.” Uch xil dalil so‘rash iborasini baland ovozda ayting. Har birini ikki xil ohangda ayting: past va baland — suhbatda ohang ham muhim.
scenes.say: Your opponent claims: “Remote workers are less productive.” Ask for evidence three different ways, aloud.
scenes.say_uz: Raqib da’vo qiladi: “Remote workers are less productive.” — “Masofaviy ishchilar kamroq unumdor.” Uch xil dalil so‘rang baland ovozda.

scenes.title: Javoblar
scenes.say_native: Javoblar: “What’s the evidence for that?” “Could you give an example?” “Where does that figure come from?” Endi bosim ostida muloyim qolishni o‘rganamiz. Uchala savol ham muloyim va aniq — professional muhokamada bemalol ishlatasiz.
scenes.say: Answers: “What's the evidence for that?” “Could you give an example?” “Where does that figure come from?” Now — staying polite under pressure.
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar: “What's the evidence for that?” “Could you give an example?” “Where does that figure come from?” Endi bosim ostida muloyim qolish.

scenes.title: Bosim ostida muloyim qolish
board: Never: “That's stupid” / “You're wrong” — attack the claim, not the person

examples.t: I understand your position — let's look at the data together.
examples.uz: Fikringizni tushunaman — keling, ma’lumotlarni birga ko‘rib chiqaylik.

scenes.say_native: Bosim ostida muloyim qolish: “I understand your position,…” — fikringizni tushunaman; “I appreciate your point,…” — nuqtangizni qadrlayman; “Let’s agree to disagree.” — kelishmaymiz, lekin hurmat qilamiz. Hech qachon shaxsiyatga o‘tmang: “That’s stupid” yoki “You’re wrong” — kishining shaxsiyatiga emas, da’vosiga hujum qiling. O‘zbek tilida ham shunday: “Fikringizni tushunaman, ammo…” Muloyimlik — zaiflik emas: ingliz tilida “with respect”, “I appreciate”, “I understand” iboralari sizning jiddiyligingizni kuchaytiradi, emasligingizni emas. G‘azab har doim kuchingizni pasaytiradi.
scenes.say: Staying polite under pressure: “I understand your position,…” “I appreciate your point,…” “Let's agree to disagree.” Never attack the person — “that's stupid” or “you're wrong” attack the individual. Attack the claim, not the character. The same rule applies in Uzbek.
scenes.say_uz: Bosim ostida muloyim qolish: “I understand your position,…” “I appreciate your point,…” “Let's agree to disagree.” Hech qachon shaxsiyatga o‘tmang — “that's stupid” yoki “you're wrong” kishiga hujum qiladi. Kishiga emas, da’vosiga hujum qiling. O‘zbek tilida ham shunday.

scenes.title: Muloyim javob tanlang
board: Best reply: a, b or c?
a) No it isn't. b) I understand the frustration — here's my evidence. c) Whatever.
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Xo‘jayiningiz gapirdi: “Your analysis is lazy.” — “Tahlilingiz dangasalarcha.” Eng yaxshi javobni tanlang: a) “No it isn’t.” b) “I understand the frustration — here’s my evidence.” c) “Whatever.” Javobingizni baland ovozda ayting va nega.
scenes.say: Your boss says: “Your analysis is lazy.” Choose the best reply — “No it isn't,” “I understand the frustration — here's my evidence,” or “Whatever.” Say your choice aloud and explain why.
scenes.say_uz: Xo‘jayiningiz deydi: “Your analysis is lazy.” — “Tahlilingiz dangasalarcha.” Eng yaxshi javobni tanlang: “No it isn't.”, “I understand the frustration — here's my evidence.” yoki “Whatever.” Javobingizni baland ovozda ayting va nega.

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: b — own the frustration, show evidence
scenes.say_native: Javoblar: b) — g‘azabni tan olasiz, dalilingizni ko‘rsatasiz — professional. A) himoyaviy, c) inkor qilish. Endi haqiqiy bahs suhbatini o‘qiymiz. Yomon ohang har doim munosabatni buzadi — grammatikangiz qanchalik yaxshi bo‘lmasin.
scenes.say: Answers: b — acknowledge the frustration and show your evidence; that's professional. a is defensive, c is dismissive. Now a real debate.
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar: b — g‘azabni tan oling va dalilingizni ko‘rsating; bu professional. A — himoyaviy, c — inkor. Endi haqiqiy bahs suhbati.

scenes.title: Tinglash: ikki nomzod — tortishuv
board: Listen: a debate about city cars
scenes.say_native: Endi ikki nomzod suhbatini tinglang — shahar markazida mashinalarni taqiqlash haqida. Ikki savol tayyorlab, keyin javoblarni tekshiramiz. Gapirgan paytda ovoz balandligi va tezligi ham muhim: past, sekin va aniq ohang sizni ishonchli ko‘rsatadi. O‘zbek tilida ham “sokin gapiruvchi — doni” degan naql bor.
scenes.say: Now listen to two candidates debating whether cars should be banned from city centres. Two questions will follow.
scenes.say_uz: Endi ikki nomzodning tortishuvini tinglang — shahar markazida mashinalarni taqiqlash. Keyin ikki savol keladi.

scenes.title: Bahs matni
board: A: Cars should be banned in city centres.
B: That would kill small businesses.
A: Evidence shows pedestrian zones boost retail by twenty percent.
B: Fair point — but delivery vehicles need access.
scenes.say_native: Tinglang. A va B o‘rtasidagi bahsni eshiting va e’tirof hamda raddiya iboralarini quloq solib ajrating. Har gapni ohang bilan tinglang: A ko‘tarilib boshlaydi, B har doim pasayib — ikki xil strategiya.
scenes.say: A: I strongly believe cars should be banned from city centres. B: I see your point, but that would kill small businesses. A: With respect — research shows pedestrian zones boost retail by twenty percent. B: Fair point. However, delivery vehicles still need access. A: I appreciate that, but electric delivery vans can work outside peak hours.
scenes.say_uz: A: Men qat’iy ishonaman — mashinalar shahar markazida taqiqlanishi kerak. B: Fikringizni tushunaman, ammo bu kichik biznesni o‘ldiradi. A: Hurmat bilan — tadqiqotlar piyoda zonalarda savdo yigirma foizga oshishini ko‘rsatadi. B: Fikringizda jon bor. Biroq yetkazib berish mashinalari kirishiga ruxsat kerak. A: Buni qadrlayman, ammo elektr yetkazib berish mashinalari tirbandlik bo‘lmagan soatlarda ishlashi mumkin.

scenes.title: Bahs savollari
board: 2. What did B concede, and what did B counter with?
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Ikki savolga javob bering: A qanday dalil keltirdi? B nima e’tirof etdi va nima raddiya berdi? Baland ovozda ingliz tilida javob bering. Yodda saqlang: dalilni qog‘ozga yozmagansiz, faqat eshitgansiz — bu eslab qolish mashqi.
scenes.say: Answer two questions aloud: What evidence did A give? What did B concede, and what did B counter with?
scenes.say_uz: Ikki savolga baland ovozda javob bering: A qanday dalil keltirdi? B nima e’tirof etdi va nima raddiya berdi?

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: A: pedestrian zones boost retail by 20%.
B: conceded the boost — countered with delivery access.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar: A dalil sifatida piyoda zonalarda savdo yigirma foizga oshishini keltirdi; B o‘z fikrini tan oldi — “Fair point” — ammo yetkazib berish masalasi bilan raddiya berdi. E’tirof-raddiya sxemasi ishladi. Endi xatolarni ko‘ramiz. Tinglashda qismlarni belgilab boring: da’vo, dalil, e’tirof, raddiya. IELTS tinglashida xuddi shu tartib so‘raladi — gapning umumiy oqimini tutsangiz, savollarga tez javob berasiz.
scenes.say: Answers: A cited research that pedestrian zones boost retail by twenty percent; B conceded the boost — “fair point” — and countered with delivery access. The concede-and-counter pattern worked. Now the mistakes.
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar: A piyoda zonalarda savdo yigirma foizga oshishini keldi; B buni tan oldi — “Fair point” — ammo yetkazib berish bilan raddiya berdi. E’tirof-raddiya sxemasi ishladi. Endi xatolar.

scenes.title: Keng tarqalgan xato: shaxsiy hujum
board: ✓ “I respectfully disagree — the evidence suggests otherwise.”
Attack the claim, not the person

examples.t: The idea is weak, not the person.

scenes.say_native: Keng tarqalgan xato: shaxsiyatga o‘tish. “You’re stupid if you think that” — ingliz tilida bu suhbatni tugatadi va sizni professional emas qiladi. To‘g‘risi: “I respectfully disagree — the evidence suggests otherwise.” — “Hurmat bilan rozi emasman — dalillar aksinchasini ko‘rsatadi.” Kishiga emas, da’vosiga hujum qiling. Endi shu xatoni to‘g‘rilang mashqi. Yana bir xato: “obviously” so‘zi suhbatdoshni pastga uradi; o‘rniga “clearly” ishlating.
scenes.say: A very common mistake: personal attacks. “You're stupid if you think that” ends the conversation and destroys your credibility. Instead: “I respectfully disagree — the evidence suggests otherwise.” Attack the claim, never the character. Now the drill.
scenes.say_uz: Juda keng tarqalgan xato: shaxsiyatga o‘tish. “You're stupid if you think that” suhbatni tugatadi va jiddingizni buzadi. To‘g‘risi: “I respectfully disagree — the evidence suggests otherwise.” — “Hurmat bilan rozi emasman — dalillar aksinchasini ko‘rsatadi.” Kishiga emas, da’vosiga hujum qiling. Endi mashq.

scenes.title: Shaxsiy hujumni qayta yozing
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Ikki shaxsiy hujumni muloyim raddiyaga aylantiring: “That’s a ridiculous idea.” va “You don’t understand anything.” Baland ovozda ayting. Har birini baland ovozda ayting va yumshoqlik darajasini his qiling.
scenes.say: Rewrite two personal attacks as polite disagreement: “That's a ridiculous idea,” and “You don't understand anything.” Say both aloud.
scenes.say_uz: Ikki shaxsiy hujumni muloyim raddiyaga aylantiring: “That's a ridiculous idea.” va “You don't understand anything.” Baland ovozda ayting.

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: “I see where you're coming from, but…”
scenes.say_native: Javoblar: “I see where you’re coming from, but the data suggests a different picture.” — “Qaerdan kelayotganingizni tushunaman, ammo ma’lumotlar boshqacha rasm ko‘rsatadi.” “Let’s look at the evidence together.” — “Keling, dalillarni birga ko‘rib chiqaylik.” Endi yakuniy vazifaga o‘tamiz. Raddiya berayotganda “however” dan keyin qisqa va aniq gap ayting: qanchalik qisqa bo‘lsa, shunchalik kuchli. Uzun va murakkab raddiya odatda ta’sirini yo‘qotadi.
scenes.say: Answers: “I see where you're coming from, but the data suggests a different picture.” And “Let's look at the evidence together.” Now the final task.
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar: “I see where you're coming from, but the data suggests a different picture.” Va “Let's look at the evidence together.” Endi yakuniy vazifa.

scenes.title: Tinglash: byudjet bahsi
board: Listen: two colleagues argue about marketing budget
scenes.say_native: Endi ikki hamkasbingizning bahsini tinglang — marketing byudjetini qayta taqsimlash haqida. E’tirof va raddiya hamda dalil so‘rash iboralarini tutib qolishga harakat qiling. Ikki savol tayyor bo‘lgandan keyin javoblarni tekshiramiz.
scenes.say: A: I strongly believe we should double the social media budget. B: I hear you, but our email campaigns convert better. A: What's the evidence for that? B: Our last three campaigns hit a four percent conversion rate. Fair point — let's split the difference: thirty percent more, not double.
scenes.say_uz: A: Men qat’iy ishonaman — ijtimoiy media byudjetini ikki barobarga oshirish kerak. B: Fikringizni eshitdim, ammo email kampaniyalarimiz yaxshiroq konvertatsiya qiladi. A: Buning dalili qanday? B: Oxirgi uchta kampaniyamiz to‘rt foiz konvertatsiya ko‘rsatdi. Fikringizda jon bor — keling, o‘rtani topamiz: ikki baravar emas, o‘ttiz foiz ko‘proq.

scenes.title: Bahs savollari: byudjet
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Ikki savolga javob bering: B qanday dalil keltirdi? Qanday murosaga kelishdi? Baland ovozda ingliz tilida javob bering, har bir javobni oddiy gapda ayting.
scenes.say: Answer two questions aloud: What evidence did B give? And what compromise did they reach in the end?
scenes.say_uz: Ikki savolga baland ovozda javob bering: B qanday dalil keltirdi? Oqibatda qanday murosaga kelishdilar?

scenes.title: Javoblar
scenes.say_native: Javoblar: B dalil sifatida oxirgi uchta email kampaniyasining to‘rt foiz konvertatsiyasini keltirdi. Murosalar esa: ikki barobar emas, o‘ttiz foiz ko‘proq. Ko‘rib turibsiz — dalil bor joyda murosaga kelish oson bo‘ladi. Endi yakuniy vazifaga o‘tamiz.
scenes.say: Answers: B cited a four percent conversion rate on the last three email campaigns. Their compromise: thirty percent more, not double. When there's evidence, compromise becomes easy. Now the final task.
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar: B oxirgi uchta email kampaniyasining to‘rt foiz konvertatsiyasini dalil qildi. Murosalar: ikki barobar emas, o‘ttiz foiz ko‘proq. Dalil bor joyda murosaga kelish oson. Endi yakuniy vazifa.

scenes.title: Yakuniy nutq: 60 soniya
board: Record yourself: state a claim, one piece of evidence, and one polite objection
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Telefoningizga oltmish soniyalik nutq yozib oling: bitta da’vo, bitta dalil va bitta muloyim e’tirozni o‘zingiz bering — “I grant that…, however…”. Baland va aniq gapiring.
scenes.say: Record sixty seconds: state one claim, one piece of evidence, and one polite objection that you raise yourself — start with “I grant that…, however…”. Speak clearly and slowly.
scenes.say_uz: Oltmish soniyalik nutq yozib oling: bitta da’vo, bitta dalil va bitta muloyim e’tirozni o‘zingiz bering — “I grant that…, however…” deb boshlang. Aniq va sekin gapiring.

scenes.title: Yakuniy vazifa: ikki tomonlama bahs
board: Pick a topic: e.g. “Should university be free?”
Write both sides, then record YOUR view (60–90 seconds)
scenes.say_native: Yakuniy vazifa: mavzu tanlang — masalan “Universitet bepul bo‘lishi kerakmi?” — va ikkala tomonning dalillarini yozing, keyin o‘z fikringizni oltmish-to‘qson soniya yozib oling. Qurilmangizga gaplang. Ikkala tomonni yozish — bahsning eng kuchli tayyorgarligi: raqibingizning dalillarini oldindan bilasiz.
scenes.say: Final task: choose a topic — for example, “Should university be free?” — write the case for both sides, then record your own view for sixty to ninety seconds.
scenes.say_uz: Yakuniy vazifa: mavzu tanlang — masalan “Universitet bepul bo‘lishi kerakmi?” — ikkala tomonning dalillarini yozing, keyin o‘z fikringizni oltmish-to‘qson soniya yozib oling.

scenes.title: Bugun nimani o‘rgandik
board: State · Support with evidence · Concede · Counter
Ask: “What's the evidence?” · Stay polite · Attack claims, not people
scenes.say_native: Xulosa. Fikr bayon qilishni, dalillar bilan qo‘llashni, e’tirof va raddiyani, dalil so‘rashni, bosim ostida muloyim qolishni va shaxsiy hujumlardan saqlanishni o‘rgandik. Keyingi darsda madaniyat va odob — ingliz tilidagi o‘zbeklarning eng ko‘p xato qiladigan joylari. Yakuniy yozuvda ikkala tomonni teng yozing: har tomondan ikki-uch dalil, keyin o‘z xulosangiz — “On balance, I believe…” shunga o‘xshash. Bu muvozanat sizning adolatli ekaningizni ko‘rsatadi. Bu ko‘nikmalar IELTS ning 7+ balli uchun ham yetarli.
scenes.say: Recap: stating opinions, supporting with evidence, conceding and countering, asking for evidence, staying polite under pressure, and attacking claims rather than people. Next time: culture and etiquette — the areas where Uzbek speakers most often slip in English.
scenes.say_uz: Xulosa: fikr bayon qilish, dalillar bilan qo‘llash, e’tirof va raddiya, dalil so‘rash, bosim ostida muloyim qolish va shaxsiy hujumlardan saqlanish. Keyingi darsda madaniyat va odob.

scenes.title: Uy vazifasi va keyingi dars
board: Homework: write both sides of a debate and record your view
Check: evidence on both sides · polite countering
Next lesson: P1-24 culture and etiquette
scenes.say_native: Uy vazifasi: tanlagan mavzuingizning ikkala tomonini yozing va o‘z fikringizni oltmish-to‘qson soniya yozib oling. Mezon: har ikki tomonda dalil bo‘lsin, yozuvda e’tirof va raddiya iboralari ishlatilgan bo‘lsin, yozuvda shaxsiy hujumlar bo‘lmasin. Keyingi darsda madaniyat va odob. Do‘stingizga bitta tarafni o‘qib bering va ishontiring — ishonmasa, dalillaringizni qayta ko‘ring.
scenes.say: Homework: write both sides of your chosen debate and record your view for sixty to ninety seconds. Success criteria: evidence on both sides, concede-and-counter language in the text, no personal attacks. Next time: culture and etiquette.
scenes.say_uz: Uy vazifasi: tanlangan mavzuning ikkala tomonini yozing va o‘z fikringizni oltmish-to‘qson soniya yozib oling. Mezon: ikkala tomonda dalillar, e’tirof va raddiya iboralari, shaxsiy hujumlar yo‘q. Keyingi darsda madaniyat va odob.

homework_uz: Uy vazifasi: tanlangan mavzuning ikkala tomonini yozing va o‘z fikringizni oltmish-to‘qson soniya yozib oling. Mezon: ikkala tomonda dalillar bo‘lsin, e’tirof va raddiya iboralari ishlatilgan bo‘lsin, shaxsiy hujumlar bo‘lmasin. Keyingi darsda madaniyat va odob.

options: I accept your point, at least partly

a debatable position you will defend

the debate is over, you lost
